- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.4) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often over-estimates continuation; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5) and price is trending upward, model under-reacts; add 1–3% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven reversal.
- Model frequently under-estimates true price range in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; widen forecast range by 2–5% for high-sentiment periods.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast upward.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by > 5% in first 7 days, assume momentum bias; reduce subsequent forecast by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment with low volatility, model tends to over-smooth; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture mean reversion bias.
